question: When a substance combines with O₂, it gets:
solution:
The correct answer is __**oxidised.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A substance that combines with oxygen is said to be "**oxidised**__."
 
• In order to prevent __**oxidation**__, materials can be coated with substances that inhibit oxidation, such as paint or oil.
 
• This process typically releases energy, in the form of** heat and light**.
 
• **Oxidation reactions **are a crucial part of many natural processes, including **respiration and combustion**.
 
• Oxidation can also have negative effects, such as **rusting of metal and rotting of organic materials**.

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• A substance combines with oxygen through a chemical reaction known as **combustion**.
 
• This reaction typically releases energy in the form of **heat and light.**__
 
• The resulting compound is typically a compound containing oxygen,** such as water or carbon dioxide.**
 
• __**Combustion reaction**__s require fuel and an **oxidizer**, with oxygen being the most common **oxidizer**.
 
• Complete combustion results in the production of** CO₂ and H₂O**, while incomplete combustion can produce harmful by-products such as **carbon monoxide.**
